subject.title: feat(memory): default cross-conversation recall for personal installs

question: Should inferred personal-install recall be allowed to default on only after runtime channel DM isolation and effective `memorySearch.enabled` are available to the resolver, or should the product retain explicit opt-in until that contract exists?
rationale: The safe default depends on whether route-time channel isolation is an authoritative privacy boundary, which cannot be inferred safely from persisted config alone.

options.title: Retain explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the shipped default-off behavior until a single authoritative runtime policy input can distinguish personal from isolated traffic.

options.title: Define runtime-aware defaulting
options.body: Approve the default flip only after the runtime scope and effective memory-search state are carried into the resolver with focused privacy regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Retain explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the shipped default-off behavior until a single authoritative runtime policy input can distinguish personal from isolated traffic.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history identifies this person as the strongest available routing candidate for the original recall/privacy contract.
